title: Israeli Airstrike Kills Family of Three Including 6-Month-Old Infant in Nuseirat Refugee Camp
detail: An Israeli air raid struck an apartment building in Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza in the early morning hours of May 24, 2026, killing three members of a single family: Mohammad Abu Mallouh (father), Alaa Zaqlan (mother), and their 6-month-old infant son Osama. Approximately 10 additional people were wounded in the strike. Bodies and wounded were transferred to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir el-Balah. The Nuseirat camp is one of the original 1948 refugee camps, originally housing Palestinians displaced during the Nakba, now among the most densely populated areas of central Gaza. The strike continues the pattern documented by the UN Security Council of near-daily Israeli operations inside Gaza under the October 2025 ceasefire — with the post-ceasefire Palestinian death toll now exceeding 940+. The killing of an infant drew condemnation from UNRWA, UNICEF, and UN human rights officials who noted the pattern of families with young children being killed.

media.caption: Israeli airstrike kills family of three including 6-month-old infant Osama in Nuseirat refugee camp — May 24, 2026

title: ICC Expected to Issue Five New Arrest Warrants Against Israeli Officials Including Defense Minister, IDF Chief
detail: Reports emerged on May 24, 2026 — corroborated by multiple Israeli and international media outlets — that the International Criminal Court was expected to issue five new sealed arrest warrants against senior Israeli officials: Defense Minister Israel Katz, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir, and Southern Command Chief Maj.-Gen. Yaniv Asor. The ICC's office officially denied that warrants had been issued, consistent with the court's standard practice of maintaining secrecy on active warrant proceedings. The prospective warrants would add to the two confirmed active warrants already held by former Prime Minister Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Gallant, both issued in November 2024 for war crimes and crimes against humanity. The Smotrich application was reported to be the first-ever ICC warrant to include an apartheid charge as a standalone count. Israeli officials called the anticipated warrants 'a declaration of war' and signaled non-compliance. The warrants — if issued — would legally require all 124 ICC member states to arrest the listed individuals on entry, creating major constraints on diplomatic travel for the named officials.

media.caption: ICC reportedly to issue five new warrants targeting Israeli Defense Minister, Finance Minister, Security Minister, and IDF chiefs — May 24, 2026
